title: Saving for post-secondary education
learningObjectives: Understand how time and compound interest can increase savings
Understand the value of starting early to save for future goals
Calculate future value from principal, annual rate, compounding frequency and time

explanations.text: Compound interest means earning interest on both saved money and on interest already earned.

evidence.quote: Compound interest: When you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.
Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

explanations.text: A principal of $1,000 earning 5 percent once a year grows to $1,050 after one year and $1,102.50 after two years.

evidence.quote: So let's say you invest $1,000 (your principal) and it earns 5 percent (interest rate) once a year (the compounding frequency).
After the first year, you would have $1,050—your original principal, plus 5 percent, or $50.

explanations.text: Starting sooner and increasing compounding frequency, interest rate, or principal helps savings grow faster.

evidence.quote: The sooner you start saving in an account that pays interest, the faster your money can grow.
Increasing the compounding frequency or your interest rate or adding to your principal can help your savings grow even faster.
